turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so I'd like to start with why a zero went into the gradebook before anyone called me.
Okay. Let's look at the essay.
Fine. Which essay, and what exactly are you putting in front of me? I'm writing down whatever you show me.
You're very sharp, you know that?
Don't manage me, Hale. You still haven't answered why the zero went in before anyone called me.
No, really. You caught the timestamp issue in thirty seconds. That's sharp.
Flattery won't move me, Hale. I didn't say anything about a timestamp. I asked why the zero went in before anyone called me, and I'm still waiting for that answer.
I just keep thinking, someone that sharp must see why I had to flag it.
"Had to." Nobody makes you enter a zero before you've spoken to the student or his parent. Check your own procedure, Hale: contact comes before any mark goes in.
